## VSiN on this hire — The Coaching Carousel Never Stops

*Adam Burke, p. 35. GUIDE CONTENT — TTW reference notes summarising the guide's assessment; the judgement is the guide's.*

Adam Burke frames the hire as a reversal of approach: going the defensive route didn't work, so Oregon State has gone in the other direction. He is sympathetic to the predecessor — Tyler Bray really walked into a brutal situation after Jonathan Smith left, as the Beavers floated around like a feather in the wind when the Pac-12 dissolved, playing as a Pac-12 team in name only, mostly facing a Mountain West schedule and even playing fellow orphan Washington State twice last season, before going 5-14. He then introduces Shephard, a longtime wide receivers coach most recently with Kalen DeBoer at both Washington and Alabama, and notes that like Washington State, Oregon State should be ready to invest in the programme with a conference to call home again. His reservation is precise: Shephard has never been more than a co-OC or assistant head coach and is now a head coach looking to install a dramatically different offense.
